sensor.polarization: HH (co-pol, better water/land contrast than HV)

study_box.note: All areas are measured within this study box only.

clipping_note: KRS reservoir extends west to ~76.35°E but our NISAR frame starts at ~76.45°E. The western inflow tails (Hemavathi/Cauvery confluence) are outside the frame. Estimated coverage: ~55-65% of the full reservoir.

validation.confidence: MODERATE. Shoreline shape matches optical imagery. Areas are plausible for the visible portion of KRS. Cannot verify absolute accuracy without ground truth or coincident optical imagery for the same dates. Wind roughening may cause 2-4 dB omission error on windy days.

methodology.threshold_rationale: Calibrated -16.0 dB. Over KRS reservoir, open water HH backscatter ranges from -16.2 to -20 dB due to wind roughening and surface capillary waves, while surrounding land is brighter (-11.0 to -13.3 dB). -16.0 dB reliably preserves the contiguous reservoir body across both windy monsoon and calm post-monsoon conditions while preventing leakage into surrounding agricultural fields.
methodology.hh_vs_hv: HV median is ~-19 to -20 dB, too close to water threshold for reliable separation. HH has 8+ dB contrast between water (-20 to -25 dB) and land (-8 to -12 dB). HH is used.

change_analysis.key_finding: Between 23 Nov 2025 and 06 Nov 2026 (same post-monsoon season and viewing geometry), detected water spread contracted by 17.31 km² (-22.2%) from 77.93 km² to 60.62 km² within the study box, driven by 18.03 km² of shoreline drawdown over a persistent 54.98 km² permanent core.
change_analysis.note: All statistics measured within study box only.

ground_truth_validation.capacity_basis: Reported storage percentages reference 49.452 TMC Gross Storage Capacity at FRL 124.80 ft (dead storage: 4.38 TMC, live storage capacity: 45.07 TMC). Note that media reports differ: some cite percentage of Gross Capacity (49.45 TMC) and others of Live Capacity (45.07 TMC).
ground_truth_validation.august_surface_sensitivity_hypothesis: A 4.92 km² open-water patch near the dam is detected in Nov '25 and Nov '26 but missed in Aug '26. Empirical analysis reveals August water backscatter is +1.1 to +1.2 dB brighter (median -15.68 dB vs -16.93 dB in Nov '25), placing 75% of patch pixels in the -16 to -14 dB range. This elevation is hypothesized to stem from monsoonal surface roughness (wind capillary waves or rain agitation), making threshold classification highly sensitive.

ground_truth_validation.concordance_statement: Confirmed: As reservoir level recedes from near-full capacity (~123 ft) past ~102–109 ft down to ~98 ft, detected surface water area decreases monotonically from 77.93 km² -> 62.72 km² -> 60.62 km² (within study box).

data_and_limits: Spatial Truncation: The study box clips ~40% of the reservoir's full water-spread area (~45% of linear E-W reach west of 76.450°E), capturing ~60% of FRL (77.93 km² of ~129.5 km² published FRL spread). All statistics apply strictly within the study box.
Sparse Temporal Sampling: Only three cloud-penetrating NISAR Track 12 GCOV acquisitions exist across 2025-2026.
Threshold Physics: Fixed backscatter threshold (-16.0 dB) is sensitive to capillary surface roughening from wind or rain, which raises water backscatter.
Ground Truth Validation: Level data from official KSNDMC / CWC bulletins confirms monotonic agreement between physical gauge level and radar water spread.
green_patch_near_dam: The green (seasonal gain) patch near the dam (~76.57°E, 12.44°N, ~1.5 km north of dam wall along the eastern embayment) represents ~1.19 km² where backscatter shifted from -15.5 to -15.8 dB in Nov 2025 to -16.2 to -16.5 dB in Nov 2026. Physical & radar analysis: This reflects two coupled factors: (1) True seasonal shoreline advance and shallow water inundation along the eastern bay; and (2) Radar interaction with topography: steep rocky embankments and dam structures cause corner reflection / double-bounce artifacts that brighten nearshore water by 1-3 dB, placing marginal pixels right around the -16 dB threshold. We treat this as a known SAR boundary effect rather than a large physical flood event.
